stage1.impression: A symmetrical, very dark room where two glowing pink-red speakers sit in a dark wooden niche, with smooth green tub chairs and a smoked ball lamp in the foreground. At 1:1 it reads as a real-time or game render: the speaker faces are blown flat pink, the niche looks like dark bathroom tile with even grout, the 'carpet' is a featureless grey that reads as concrete, the velvet has no pile or sheen, and the top third of the frame is empty black. The specific idea (a raised green zone with every seat facing a speaker altar) does come through, but a magazine would not run it as a photograph of a specific place. As shot it reads as a generic CG lounge.

Frame lum_median between 22 and 40 (now 12.6) with the ceiling and upper walls holding detail rather than empty black
The carpet reads as green wool with visible pile, not grey concrete (g_median > r_median in the floor band [100,340,600,400], now r35 g32 b31)
The end-grain niche reads as oak blocks with grain and tone variation from block to block, not a uniform dark tile grid
The velvet chairs show pile and sheen (a lighter rim where they turn from the light), not smooth vinyl
No blown white screen slab at the left frame edge
A seated, slightly off-axis viewpoint and one sign of life in the foreground (a glass on the hex table)

defects.what: Left speaker face clipped 11.2%, flat salmon-pink glow with no depth through the acrylic; edge of the cabinet is a hard 1 px CG step
Right speaker face clipped 12.1%, same flat pink glow
Speaker top section is a murky dark red blob (lum 16.6) next to the blown face below it: tonally broken
End-grain niche reads as a regular square tile grid with uniform dark joints, lum 14 with a range of only 15: no grain, no variation between blocks
Teal light cones above each speaker on the felt read as nightclub uplighting
Screen at the left edge is a near-white slab (lum 172), cut by the frame and pulling the eye
Ceiling band is empty black (lum 6), no detail and no atmosphere
Floor reads as grey smooth concrete (r35 g32 b31), not green wool carpet; a smooth CG surface
Velvet tub chair back reads as smooth plastic or leather, with no pile or sheen
Second Orb lamp cut by the bottom edge, an awkward tangent
Dead-centre symmetric composition at standing height; no props or sign of life in this frame

changes.problem: The speakers, the hero, are blown to a flat pink glow, so the tint, the batts and the horn don't read as tinted acrylic.

change.setting: on each Ember speaker 4 x area, W/m2 at the target; the altar 2 x spot
change.to: 2.0 W/m2; altar 50.0 W, cone 28 -> 22 deg aimed at the plinth tops so the speaker is lit from outside and glows from within

changes.expected: The speaker face holds a saturated deep red with the white batts and the resin horn visible through it, and its edges catch a polished highlight

changes.problem: The frame is too dark overall: the median is half the floor of a readable night interior and the room around the altar is lost.

change.to: 1.6 (about +0.7 stop), applied together with c1 so the speakers don't clip again

changes.expected: The niche, the walls and the chairs come up into readable low key while the speakers stay below clipping

changes.problem: The zone's carpet renders as neutral grey smooth concrete, so the green zone loses its floor and the floor reads as CG.

evidence.measured: r35 g32 b31, lum_range 42 with no texture visible at 1:1

change.setting: the carpet's finish (material tone and roughness)
change.to: the zone's bottle green as specified, roughness 0.9 to 1.0, a sheen layer of about 0.3 and a fine wool-loop bump so it takes the Orbs' pools softly

changes.expected: The floor reads as deep green wool with soft pools of light under the tables

changes.problem: The end-grain oak niche reads as a dark square tile grid, which says bathroom, not crafted timber.

evidence.measured: lum_median 14.1, lum_range 15.3, regular joints visible in the 3x crop

change.setting: the oak's stain and finish on the end-grain blocks
change.from: a single uniform dark stain with prominent dark joints
change.to: a value that varies from block to block by +/-15%, visible growth rings and checks in each block, joints half as dark, roughness 0.6; plus the altar spots' wider spill (c1) grazing it from above

changes.expected: The niche reads as warm brown end-grain with texture and a soft gradient falling off from the speakers

changes.problem: The velvet tub chairs read as smooth green plastic, with no pile, sheen or softness.

evidence.measured: lum_median 20, r5 g24 b20, flat gradient with no rim sheen in the 2x crop

change.to: a sheen of 0.8 with sheen roughness 0.4, roughness 0.85 and a fine pile normal, so the edges turned from the Orbs pick up a lighter green rim

changes.expected: The chair backs show the bright edges and dark faces of velvet, and the foreground reads as soft and cozy

changes.problem: The screen at the left edge is a near-white slab cut by the frame, the brightest large area after the speakers.
changes.expected: The screen sits as a dim panel at the edge and stops competing with the altar

changes.problem: The ceiling and upper frame are empty black and the air has no atmosphere, so the room reads as a void, not a room at night.
changes.expected: A faint glow around the altar spots and the speakers and some separation in the ceiling band, with the pools of light still distinct

changes.problem: The standing, dead-centre, symmetric view with an empty foreground reads as a showroom render, not a magazine photograph of a lived-in room.

evidence.measured: camera z 1.35 m on the zone axis; second Orb cut at the bottom edge; no props in frame

change.to: seated height z 1.1, moved about 0.5 m off axis to the right ([11.6, 2.0, 1.1]), lens 35 mm with the aim kept on the best seat's line; add a rocks glass and a record sleeve on the foreground hex table; keep the second Orb fully in or fully out of the frame

changes.expected: A seated listener's view with the pair slightly asymmetric, less empty ceiling, and a sign of life in the foreground

out_of_scope.request: Make the room's surfaces neutral so the Ember red is the frame's only saturated colour
out_of_scope.why: The card fixes the zone and its bottle-green colour as the room's design; the green competes with the red but can't be changed here

out_of_scope.request: Tone down the speaker top section's dark red against its bright face
out_of_scope.why: This is partly the speaker's own construction and tint (fixed); c1 should balance it through light alone
